provenance_note: Every `source` here is the attribution this repository already carried, in docs/SCIENCE_CITATIONS.md, registry/INCONSISTENCIES.md or the module comments. The primary literature was NOT re-read while compiling this file, so a `source` records who the value is attributed to and not that the attribution was checked. `status` is the claim that matters: it is assigned from whether the cited work covers THIS case - short oligos, this buffer, this temperature - rather than from whether a citation exists at all.

statuses.measured: the cited work reports this value for a case the model applies it to
statuses.estimated: extrapolated from cited data taken at another temperature, on longer DNA, or in another buffer
statuses.empirical: chosen so the model behaves plausibly; no source reports it
statuses.assumed: a modelling decision with a stated reason and no supporting measurement
statuses.absent: no model computes this effect; the code must not report zero for it

records.sequence_domain: any length; the model is additive over stacks
records.temperature_domain: reference state; Tm follows from dH and dS
records.uncertainty: not stated per stack in the source

records.units: mM sodium equivalent per sqrt(mM magnesium)
records.buffer_domain: the equivalence is reported for PCR-range magnesium
records.notes: Estimated rather than measured for this application because SWGA runs at 10 mM magnesium, well above the PCR range the equivalence was characterised over, and because free magnesium is lower than total: dNTPs chelate it roughly 1:1, so 10 mM total with 1.6 mM dNTPs leaves nearer 8.4 mM free. The code applies total, not free.

records.temperature_range_note: The only one of the 25 records whose prose states a RANGE rather than a point, so it is the only one this check can act on: 11 give a single reference point and 13 give no number. Refusing on an unstated domain would turn a gap in the evidence into a gap in the tool.

Half-wired: the coefficient reaches the Tm path but the mechanistic model never reads it, and it is absent from the additive interaction map and from the range validator.

No Tm term exists. Measured in this repository on 2026-09-21: a 12-mer at 10 percent glycerol returns the same effective Tm as at 0 percent, to the last digit, while the value is range-validated to 0-15 percent and printed in the condition summary. The literature expects a real destabilisation, so this zero is an absent model rather than a result. The mechanistic model does carry glycerol enzyme-stability and speed terms, which is why the parameter is accepted at all. No coefficient is invented here; a design that sets it is refused instead.

No Tm term, deliberately. BSA acts on the enzyme and on surface adsorption, not on duplex stability, so the absence is a modelling decision with a reason rather than a gap. Distinguished from `absent` for exactly that reason.
No Tm term, deliberately. PEG is a crowding agent; its modelled effect is on association rate, not on duplex stability.

Three pairwise interaction terms exist (DMSO with magnesium, betaine with trehalose, DMSO with formamide) and all other pairs compose independently. Betaine and TMAC compose their GC-equalisation multiplicatively as 1-(1-b)(1-t), after a version in which each removed the whole GC deviation and the two were summed. Independent composition is a stated assumption, not a measurement: DMSO plus betaine is the pair three shipped examples use and it has no interaction term.

records.uncertainty: a single internal mismatch costs roughly 4-8 C depending on identity and position
records.notes: Position- and identity-independent by construction. Sites are grouped by mismatch count rather than modelled individually because per-site alignment against a 3 Gbp host is not tractable. Any specificity claim resting on this is an exact-match claim with a uniform correction, not a mismatch-discrimination measurement. This record covers the shipped `mismatch_model: uniform` path only; the position-dependent alternative carries its own records.

records.value: 64 doublets with a Watson-Crick 5' position, for INTERNAL mismatches only
records.source: SantaLucia (1998) PNAS 95:1460-1465; internal single-mismatch nearest-neighbour set
records.sequence_domain: applied to 6-18mers; the source's duplexes are longer. INTERNAL positions only: the first and last base of a duplex are outside this set, which carries no dangling-end or terminal-mismatch parameters, and the model falls back to the uniform assumed penalty there
records.buffer_domain: measured in 1 M NaCl, applied in a magnesium isothermal buffer with additives
records.temperature_domain: measured at 37 C, applied near 30 C (phi29) to 65 C (bst)
records.temperature_range_note: No checkable range is recorded, so nothing is refused on it. The reference point is 37 C and the gap to a 30 C reaction is the extrapolation this status names.
records.uncertainty: not propagated; the source reports per-doublet values without an interval here
records.notes: The table is a measurement. THIS USE of it is not: a 37 C 1 M Na+ doublet set, extrapolated to a short oligo in magnesium buffer at the reaction temperature, and converted to a melting-temperature shift by a first-order perturbation of Tm = dH/(dS + R ln C), which assumes the mismatch's cost is unchanged between 37 C and the reaction. The status describes the extrapolation, not the table. Used by core/mismatch_model.py, reachable through `mismatch_model: position-dependent` and off by default. Position enters through the flanking stacks rather than a position index. The nearest-neighbour rotation symmetry is applied so that a mismatch's 3'-side doublet resolves to a tabulated value instead of a flat penalty. Two cases are outside the set and take the uniform penalty instead of a tabulated value: a doublet with two mismatches, because the source does not parameterise tandem mismatches, and a mismatch at EITHER TERMINUS of the duplex, because an internal set does not describe a position with one flanking stack. Applying it at a terminus anyway was measured as net STABILISING for 771 of 8,400 terminal neighbours over 1,400 random primers at three polymerases, which would have weighted a mismatched host site as well as a perfect one; at interior positions it was stabilising for 0 of 43,199. Nothing refuses a design on the temperature distance, because no threshold has a reference; the distance is reported instead, in the panel assessment's evidence, in the run manifest and once per run in the log. Whether this ranks measured outcomes better than the uniform model is the question docs/validation/2026-10-02-position-dependent-mismatch.md measures.

records.source: Innis et al. (1988) PNAS 85:9436-9440, cited in core/three_prime_stability.py as a docstring attribution only
records.sequence_domain: short oligos; the cited observation is about Taq in PCR
records.buffer_domain: not established for an isothermal magnesium buffer
records.uncertainty: the factor is a stated claim, not an interval; it could be anywhere between 0 and 1
records.notes: No measurement for a strand-displacing polymerase was found. The attribution in the repository is a docstring citation that was not re-read, and the quantity it would support is extension efficiency for Taq, not for phi29 or Bst. Separately switchable from the duplex term (`mismatch_model: position-dependent-3prime`) precisely because it is the weaker claim, so a later measurement can overturn it without touching the duplex model. What would settle it: extension yield from a primer with a single 3'-terminal mismatch against a matched control, on phi29 or EquiPhi29 at the reaction temperature, over the four mismatch identities. Until then a load computed with this rule is reported with its own mode string and this record.

Primer-primer dimer chemistry carries its own record rather than inheriting the duplex one: the quantity is a bimolecular association between two short oligos at high relative concentration, not a primer annealing to a template. Nothing has validated this floor against a reaction. At the shipped max_dimer_bp of 3 a free-energy floor decides nothing, because every pair it would reject the run-length screen already rejects.
Used for amplification-network reachability, not for coverage.

Corrected from an earlier 10,000 bp attributed to Bambara et al. (1978). docs/SCIENCE_CITATIONS.md still carries the old figure, which is why this registry exists: a prose ledger nothing checks drifts from the code it describes.

records.source: Clarke et al. (2017) Bioinformatics 33:2071-2077; Dwivedi-Yu et al. (2023) PLOS Comput Biol 19:e1010137
records.uncertainty: coverage on one saved 26-oligo panel reads 41.3 percent at 1 kb, 80.1 at 3 kb, 93.5 at 5 kb and 99.6 at 10 kb
records.notes: A DESIGN-DENSITY convention taken from sets with measured wet-lab success, not a measured extension distribution and not a physical processivity. Clarke filtered candidate sets to under 5 kb mean inter-primer spacing; Dwivedi-Yu report working sets at 1/2-5 kbp. No reading of it identifies a reach. Nothing in this repository has measured it: `calibrate-reach --bam` exists and there is no BAM here. A coverage figure quoted without its reach carries almost no information.
Same convention, nudged for the higher temperature. The nudge itself has no source.

Which allocation a reaction uses is a fact about the protocol and cannot be inferred, so it is declared on the request. Under a fixed total, adding an oligo lowers every other one's concentration and therefore its occupancy; under fixed per-oligo the total rises with the panel. The two make different predictions exactly where panel size changes.
